entries.summary: A cryptographically secure random source: its bytes are unpredictable to everyone, so they suit keys, secrets, tokens, salts and nonces. It adds no member to `IRandomSource`; it is a capability that the type system checks.
Produces uniformly distributed random bytes. Every typed value, range, shuffle and selection in this library is built on this one operation.
Fills `destination` with random bytes. An empty buffer is left as it is.
The operating system's cryptographically secure random number generator as an `ISecureRandom`. Use it wherever no beacon is wanted, such as in an air-gapped deployment.
The shared instance. The type is stateless and thread-safe, so the one instance serves every caller, and it needs no disposal.
Fills `destination` with bytes from `RandomNumberGenerator`.
Typed values, ranges, shuffles and selections over any `IRandomSource`. Every member is unbiased, and deterministic given the source's bytes.

entries.summary: Registers `TBeacon` as a singleton beacon. Each beacon class registers once, and its `IRandomnessBeacon.Name` must be unique among the registered beacons.

The secure generator, the background beacon collection and reproducible draws, composed without dependency injection, for console tools and libraries that run without a host. Keep one instance for the life of the application.

Creates a builder with default options, options set by `configure` or options bound from `configuration`. An unknown configuration key fails `BuildAsync`, so a misspelled setting is never silently ignored.
Gets the secure generator.
Gets the health of the beacon collection.
Gets the factory for reproducible draws.
Stops the beacon collection, waiting up to 30 seconds, and disposes the generator, zeroing its state. A second call does nothing.
Composes a `RandomnessHost`: add beacons with the adapters' extension members, such as `AddCurbyBeacon()`, then call `BuildAsync` once.
Gets the services the host is built from. Add what a host would add, such as a logging provider; a registration made after `BuildAsync` has no effect.
Builds the host: checks every setting, as a host does at start, and starts collecting beacon pulses in the background. With `RequireInitialPulse` set, it waits for the first pulse.
Settings for the secure generator and the beacon collector, bound from the `Randomness` configuration section.
The configuration section these options bind from by convention.
How the registered beacons are used. The default is `BeaconMode.Continuous`.
How often each beacon is asked for its latest pulse. The default is one minute, the cadence at which CURBy publishes.
The longest wait between attempts while a beacon fails; the wait doubles from `RefreshInterval` up to it, with jitter. The default is fifteen minutes.
How long one attempt to fetch a pulse may take. The default is thirty seconds.
The oldest a pulse may be, by its own timestamp, to be mixed in; an older one means a beacon or a mirror has stalled. The default is ten minutes.

signatures: public Dictionary<string, TimeSpan> MaxPulseAgeByBeacon { get; set; }
entries.summary: The oldest a pulse may be, by beacon name, in place of `MaxPulseAge`, for a beacon that publishes less often. A name that no registered beacon has fails the host at start. Empty by default.
How far a pulse's timestamp may lie ahead of this machine's clock. The default is two minutes.
Whether the host fails to start unless a beacon pulse is mixed in within `InitialPulseTimeout`. The default is `false`: a beacon outage never stops an application.
How long the host waits at start for the first pulse when `RequireInitialPulse` is set. The default is thirty seconds.
The longest any generator shard runs before it reseeds from the operating system. The default is one minute.
The most bytes any generator shard produces before it reseeds from the operating system. The default is one mebibyte.

How the library uses the registered randomness beacons. `Continuous` fetches at start and every `RefreshInterval`, `InitializeOnly` fetches until each beacon has given one pulse, and `Offline` contacts no beacon. In every mode, random values are generated locally and never wait on a beacon.

A public randomness beacon, such as CURBy: the port each vendor's adapter implements. An implementation verifies every pulse as its vendor's protocol specifies before it returns it, and throws `BeaconException` rather than return a pulse it could not verify.
Gets the name the beacon is registered under, unique among the registered beacons, such as `curby`.
Fetches and verifies the beacon's latest pulse. It throws `BeaconException` when the beacon gave no verifiable pulse.
Fetches and verifies the pulse of `round`. It throws `BeaconException`, with `BeaconError.PulseNotFound` when the round has not been published.

Why a beacon gave no usable pulse. `Unavailable` is a beacon that could not be reached, `PulseNotFound` a round it has not published, `InvalidPulse` an answer that failed verification, `StalePulse` a pulse too old or too far ahead, and `RolledBack` a round earlier than one already mixed in.

How a beacon is doing, as the collector last saw it. `Pending` is a beacon whose first fetch has not finished, `Healthy` one whose last fetch gave a verified, fresh pulse, and `Unavailable` one whose last fetch failed or whose pulse was refused. The longest context, in characters.

entries.summary: Derives the stream of `pulse` for `context`. The draw is as trustworthy as the pulse: this method verifies nothing, so pass a pulse a beacon adapter returned, or use `IVerifiableRandomFactory.CreateAsync`.
Fills `destination` with the next bytes of the stream, read as consecutive 64-byte blocks. Consume the stream from one thread, in a fixed order: values depend on the order in which they are drawn.
Zeroes the stream's buffered bytes and releases its generator. The stream cannot be read afterwards.
